sonora_ca.name: Sonora
sonora_ca.obs_note: Sonora has no NWS observing station. The readings come from the Green Spring fire-weather station, 12 miles away and about 700 ft lower.

alerts.headline: Lake Wind Advisory issued October 9 at 12:47PM PDT until October 10 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS Reno NV
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Southwest winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 40 mph. Waves
2 to 3 feet on Lake Tahoe and Pyramid Lake.

* WHERE...Greater Lake Tahoe Area, Greater Reno-Carson City-Minden
Area, and Western Nevada Basin and Range including Pyramid Lake.

* WHEN...From 5 AM to 11 PM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds and rough waves on area lakes will create
hazardous conditions for small craft.

alerts.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 9 at 11:23AM PDT until October 10 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Reno NV
alerts.description:
The National Weather Service in Reno NV has issued a Red Flag Warning
in effect from 11 AM to 9 PM PDT Saturday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zones 274 Southern Mono County, 420
Northern Sierra Front including Carson City, Douglas, Storey,
Southern Washoe, Western Lyon, and Far Southern Lassen Counties,
421 Southern Sierra Front including Alpine, Northern Mono, Southern
Lyon, and Western Mineral Counties, 423 West Humboldt Basin in
Pershing County, and 429 Lahontan Basin including Churchill and
Eastern Mineral Counties.

* TIMING...From 11 AM to 9 PM PDT Saturday.

* WINDS...Southwest winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts 35 to 45 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimum Humidity between 14 to 22 percent.

* DURATION...3 to 6 hours.

* IMPACTS...The combination of gusty winds and prolonged dry
conditions, even in areas where humidity may not be as low, can
cause fires to rapidly grow in size and intensity before first
responders can contain them.

alerts.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued October 9 at 12:35PM PDT until October 9 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with high temperatures near 110
degrees and overnight lows between 80 and 85 degrees. This will
yield at least major Heat Risk, impacting anyone without adequate
cooling and hydration. For the Wind Advisory, south winds 25 to 35
mph with gusts up to 60 mph expected.

* WHERE...Elevations in Death Valley National Park below 2000 feet.

* WHEN...For the Extreme Heat Warning, until 8 PM PDT this evening.
For the Wind Advisory, from 2 PM Saturday to 5 AM PDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Heat-related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Gusty winds will blow around unsecured
objects. Tree limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may
result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There will likely be a lull in the winds from
late Saturday night through Sunday morning before winds increase
once again Sunday afternoon.

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued October 9 at 12:25PM PDT until October 12 at 5:00AM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southeast California, including the following
areas, Death Valley National Park and Western Mojave Desert and
south central Nevada, including the following area, Esmeralda and
Central Nye County.

* WHEN...From Saturday afternoon through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Incoming tropical moisture will lead to widespread shower and
thunderstorm activity, some of which may cause flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
